fact: Firestone requires any contractor doing business in the town to hold a Town contractor license, renewed every calendar year, with a general liability insurance certificate that lists the Town, and its Class C license, which names subcontractors and tradesmen too, covers landscaping, sod layers and sprinkler systems.
quote: Any contractor wishing to do business in the Town of Firestone must complete the Contractor License Application. … Contractor licenses are issued for each calendar year and must be renewed annually. Proof of Workers Compensation Insurance (if required) General Liability Certificate of Insurance listing the Town as the certificate holder AND additional insured. … Class C Building contractor, sub-contractor or tradesman $50 … Landscaping only … Sod layers Sprinkler system
source_label: Town of Firestone, Planning & Development: Contractor Licenses
notes: Read 2026-09-25. The page lists four classes (A, B, C, Electrician); Class C's examples include 'Landscaping only', 'Sod layers' and 'Sprinkler system'. Turf is not named in any class; the page does not say which class a turf-only company holds. The page also says the Town verifies state licenses for plumbers and electricians.

fact: From January 1, 2027, Greeley's Building Inspection Department will require a City of Greeley contractor license before a contractor applies for permits or starts work that department regulates, for general and specialty trades alike, and the city's August 10, 2026 announcement does not mention landscaping or turf.
quote: The City of Greeley Building Inspection Department will require contractors to have a City of Greeley contractor license starting January 1, 2027. … All contractors must have a valid City of Greeley contractor license before they: Apply for permits Start construction work Make alterations or repairs Perform demolition regulated by the Building Inspection Department … The rule applies to all applicable trades, including general contractors and specialty trade contractors. … Contractors without a valid City license may have their permit denied or be ordered to stop work.
source_label: City of Greeley news release, Contractor License Required for Permits in Greeley Starting January 1, 2027 (Aug. 10, 2026)
notes: Read 2026-09-25. The rule is tied to Building Inspection permits; single-family turf in Greeley is not a building-permit item today, so a page may say it reaches a turf job only where part of the job needs such a permit. Re-check once it takes effect for any published list of trades.

fact: Colorado's plumbing law requires a plumbing license to install or remove a backflow prevention device, exempts inspecting, testing and repairing one, needs no plumbing license for work on lawn sprinkling systems equipped with backflow preventers, and lets a homeowner do plumbing on their own home.
quote: (2) Nothing in this article 155 requires an individual to hold a license to perform plumbing work on the individual's own property or residence … (4) Individuals who are engaged in inspecting, testing, or repairing backflow prevention devices are exempt from licensure under this article 155. Individuals who engage in the installation or removal of backflow prevention devices are not exempt from licensure under this article 155 … (6) (a) Nothing in this article 155 requires a plumbing license, registration, or permit to perform: (I) The installation, extension, alteration, or maintenance, including the related water piping and the indirect waste piping, of domestic appliances equipped with backflow preventers, including lawn sprinkling systems
source_label: C.R.S. 12-155-118, Exemptions (Plumbers Practice Act, Colorado Revised Statutes 2025 printout posted by the State Plumbing Board)
notes: Read 2026-09-25 in the 'Plumbers Practice Act.pdf' linked from https://dpo.colorado.gov/Plumbing/Laws (uncertified 2025 printout). The homeowner exemption in (2) does not reach property built for sale or rental. The fire-suppression exception in (4) is left out as irrelevant here.

fact: Colorado's Division of Professions and Occupations tells homeowners that a hired plumbing contractor is responsible for the plumbing permit, that it violates state law for anyone other than the homeowner who is not a registered plumbing contractor to install a plumbing project on their property, and that homeowners insurance may not cover damage caused by someone without liability insurance.
quote: If you are a homeowner hiring an Electrical Contractor or Plumbing Contractor, you contractor is responsible for obtaining the required permit(s). As the homeowner, you should not continue with the permit application process. Be aware that it is a violation of state law for an individual (other than the homeowner) that is not a registered Electrical or Plumbing Contractor to install an electrical or plumbing project on your property. In addition, homeowner's insurance may not cover the costs of repair for the work performed by anyone without liability insurance who causes damage to your home. … Residential Installation - Fixture count for the installation (traps, water hammer, arrestors, backflow preventers, water heaters, fuel gas outlets, and fuel gas pressure regulators).
source_label: Colorado Division of Professions and Occupations, Electrical and Plumbing Permits: Notice to Homeowner
notes: Read 2026-09-25. 'you contractor' is the page's own typo. The state issues and inspects plumbing permits only where no local plumbing inspection program exists; a town with its own program issues its own.

fact: Colorado's Attorney General says general contractors must pay the subcontractors they hire, lists unlicensed work, failing to pay subcontractors, refusing to pull required local permits and door-to-door selling after hailstorms among signs of contractor fraud, and tells homeowners to check local licensing with their city or county, search state electrical and plumbing licenses through the Department of Regulatory Agencies, get at least three bids and check the Better Business Bureau.
quote: General contractors have a legal responsibility to do work they’ve agreed to perform and pay the subcontractors they have hired. … Performing unlicensed work. … Failure to pay subcontractors or failing to set aside money for subcontractors. … Going door-to-door looking for customers, especially after a hailstorm or other severe weather event or a natural disaster. … Refusing to pull required local permits. … Check with your city or county to make sure the general contractor is licensed to work in your area. Licenses to perform electrical or plumbing work are regulated by the state and you can search for them with the Department of Regulatory Agencies … Arrange bids or estimates from at least three businesses before signing any agreements. Check with the Better Business Bureau to see if the business has any complaints filed against them. … If you believe a contractor is defrauding you, attempt to work things out with the contractor first and document these attempts. … If you can’t solve the problem and believe you may be the victim of a scam or fraud, file a complaint with the Colorado Attorney General’s Office
source_label: Colorado Attorney General, Stop Fraud Colorado: Contractor Fraud
notes: Read 2026-09-25. The page's first sentence is split across span tags in the HTML; the quote is the rendered text.

fact: The FTC lists a contractor asking you to get the required building permits, knocking on doors or offering leftover materials among the signs of a home improvement scam, and advises confirming a contractor's license with state or county government, asking for proof of insurance, getting several written estimates that describe the work, materials, completion date and price, and not automatically taking the lowest bid.
quote: Scammers knock on your door looking for business because they are “in the area.” Scammers say they have materials left over from a previous job. … Scammers ask you to get any required building permits. … Check with your state or county government to confirm a contractor’s license, and ask the contractor for proof of insurance. … Get multiple estimates. A written estimate should include a description of the work to be done, materials, completion date, and the price. Don’t automatically choose the lowest bidder. And ask for an explanation if there’s a big difference among the estimates. … First try to resolve it with the contractor. … Request a return receipt, so you can prove that the company got your letter.
source_label: Federal Trade Commission, Consumer Advice: How To Avoid a Home Improvement Scam (July 2022)

fact: Colorado's Secretary of State says Good Standing means only that a business's statutory filings are met, that the office neither verifies those filings nor regulates business practices, and that its records do not tell you whether a business is reputable, pointing to the Better Business Bureau's reliability reports.
quote: “Good Standing” status means that statutory filing requirements have been met with our office. However, this office does not review or verify information submitted in those filings. This office also does not regulate or investigate business practices or operations. … Q7. Do your records tell me if a business is reputable? A7. No. The Secretary of State's office is only a filing registry of businesses. The Better Business Bureau (BBB) provides business reliability reports, dispute resolution, and charity reviews.
source_label: Colorado Secretary of State, Business FAQs: Certificate of Good Standing

fact: The Colorado Secretary of State's business database searches by business name, trade name, ID or document number, and the office says it is only a filing registry that cannot certify whether a business is operating legally.
quote: Search by business name, trademark, trade name, ID or document number … Disclaimer: The Secretary of State's Office acts as a filing registry for businesses. This office lacks the authority to certify if a business is operating legally.
source_label: Colorado Secretary of State, Business Database Search
notes: Read 2026-09-25 at coloradosos.gov; the same page at sos.state.co.us returns 403 to automated fetches.

fact: Northern Colorado has its own Better Business Bureau office, the BBB Serving Northern Colorado and Wyoming, a non-profit whose stated mission is to advance marketplace trust.
quote: The Better Business Bureau Serving Northern Colorado and Wyoming is a non-profit organization with a mission to advance marketplace trust by creating a marketplace where buyers and sellers can trust each other.
source_label: BBB Serving Northern Colorado and Wyoming, office page
notes: The page sits behind a bot check that blocks curl and headless browsers; the quote is the page's own description text, read 2026-09-25 through a fetch. Re-read the body in a browser.

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council tells buyers to check an installer's references and complaint record, to visit its installations, particularly ones several years old, and to get several references and several projects from the past several years to inspect in person.
quote: Research the synthetic grass manufacturer and installation company with whom you may contract. Carefully check their warranty, website, references, and complaint record with the Better Business Bureau and the local consumer affairs office. Visit some of their installations, particularly those that are several years old. … The installation contractor should provide you with the following: Several references you should talk with, and several projects completed during the past several years that you should personally inspect;
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Considerations When Buying Synthetic Grass for Landscape Use (September 2013)
notes: Read 2026-09-25: Summary of Critical Guidelines (p. 1) and Guidelines for Prequalifying and Selecting a Professional Contractor (p. 5).

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council says an installer should give buyers a certificate of insurance showing workers' compensation and general liability coverage, including products and completed operations, and contact details for the person and company who answer service issues.
quote: Complete contact information for the person and company responsible for responding to customer questions, and service issues; … A Certificate of Insurance evidencing Workers’ Compensation and General Liability Insurance, including products/completed operations coverage.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Considerations When Buying Synthetic Grass for Landscape Use (September 2013)

fact: The Synthetic Turf Council tells buyers to keep the turf sample they choose, get a written commitment that it is the product delivered, and check the delivered rolls, including their country of origin, against it before installation.
quote: Keep the synthetic grass sample you select, and compare it before installation to the product that is delivered. … The turf sample should identify where the turf was manufactured, e.g., USA or China. When the turf rolls are received, make sure to check the shipping label on the turf rolls and bill of lading to verify that the country of origin is the same as was originally represented; … A written commitment that the sample you select when you sign the contract will be the product that is delivered for installation.
source_label: Synthetic Turf Council, Considerations When Buying Synthetic Grass for Landscape Use (September 2013)

fact: The Colorado Department of Agriculture's online applicator search looks up businesses holding a commercial pesticide applicator license and returns only current, valid licenses.
quote: Businesses holding a License or Registration or individuals with a Qualified Supervisor, Certified Operator or a Private Applicator License can now be verified online. … Business: will search for Commercial Applicators Licenses, and Limited Commercial and Public Applicator Registrations … This search will only produce current valid licenses or registrations, expired licenses will not show in the results.
source_label: Colorado Department of Agriculture, Pesticide Applicator Search
